title: Align WebFetch tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all WebFetch improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go WebFetch has the same public name and the basic url/prompt fetch surface, and it already contains partial parity work for HTML-to-Markdown conversion, preapproved hosts, a pluggable summariser, binary persistence, domain-info preflight, and provider-native experiments. It is still not implementation-equivalent to the TS reference. The largest remaining gaps are in permission/approval lifecycle, default domain-info security semantics, redirect policy and redirect output, cache key/value/lifecycle, prompt application and cancellation behavior, binary handling, model-facing output schema, HTTP/body-limit behavior, preapproved-host matching, and test coverage that currently exercises helpers more than the production Execute path.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Per-call WebFetch permission decisions and rule updates are missing in Go
improvement_points.description: TS WebFetch is permission-aware before execution: preapproved hosts allow automatically, deny/ask/allow rules are matched by domain:<hostname>, and ask decisions include localSettings rule suggestions. Go WebFetch only has static AllowedDomains/DisallowedDomains slices injected at registry setup and a direct Execute path; there is no tool permission hook, no ask decision, no per-call ruleContent generation, and no localSettings update lifecycle. This affects both security parity and the user's ability to approve a domain once and reuse that rule.

improvement_points.title: Domain-info preflight defaults, response shape, and failure semantics differ
improvement_points.description: TS performs a domain blocklist preflight by default unless skipWebFetchPreflight is set, parses the Anthropic response as can_fetch, caches only allowed hosts, blocks can_fetch=false, and treats check failures as user-visible failures. Go makes preflight opt-in, parses a different blocked boolean shape, ignores lookup errors in Execute, and fail-opens/caches not-blocked on transport or non-2xx failures. That is a material security and robustness divergence.

improvement_points.title: Redirect safety policy and redirect result format are not TS-equivalent
improvement_points.description: TS follows only permitted redirects: same protocol, same port, no redirect credentials, and same host after adding/removing www., with a maximum of 10 hops. Cross-host redirects are returned as a detailed REDIRECT DETECTED message instructing the model to call WebFetch again, and they are not cached as fetched content. Go uses a 5-hop limit, sameOriginRedirect ignores protocol, port, and userinfo, and cross-host redirects become a terse 'REDIRECT N: a -> b' summary that is cached as the final result.

improvement_points.title: The production cache caches final prompt results by URL+prompt instead of raw fetched content by URL
improvement_points.description: TS caches fetched markdown/content metadata by original URL before prompt application, with 15-minute TTL and 50MB LRU byte accounting; different prompts for the same URL reuse the fetched page but re-run prompt application. Go Execute uses the legacy searchCache, keys by url+prompt, stores rendered summary strings, caches redirect and binary markers, and does not use the typed WebFetchCache that has TTL/byte-cap lifecycle tests. This changes network behavior, prompt reapplication behavior, stored metadata, and clear-cache lifecycle parity.

improvement_points.title: Prompt application is optional and falls back silently instead of matching the TS secondary-model path
improvement_points.description: TS applies the user's prompt with queryHaiku for every non-preapproved-short-markdown response and propagates secondary-model or abort failures. Go only calls the summariser when WebFetchTool.Summariser is manually configured, registry setup does not configure one, and Execute silently falls back to keyword-overlap extraction when the summariser is absent or returns an error. This means default Go behavior is not the TS 'process content with the prompt using a small, fast model' path.

improvement_points.title: Cancellation during prompt application can be swallowed by the Go fallback path
improvement_points.description: TS threads AbortController through fetch and prompt application, then explicitly throws AbortError if the signal is aborted after the secondary model call. Go threads context to the summariser, but Execute ignores any summariser error and falls back to local keyword extraction. If the context is canceled during summarisation but the HTTP fetch already succeeded, Go can still return a non-error heuristic result instead of aborting the tool call.

improvement_points.title: Binary responses return only a marker in Go instead of being summarized with an appended saved-file note
improvement_points.description: TS persists binary content when detected, but still decodes the raw buffer as UTF-8, passes the decoded content through the normal markdown/prompt path, and appends a note that the binary content was also saved to disk. Go detects binary content, persists it, caches a marker, and returns immediately without applying the prompt or providing a summary. This is a visible functional and output-structure mismatch for PDFs and other binaries.

improvement_points.title: Go model-facing result and schema do not expose the TS WebFetch output object
improvement_points.description: TS WebFetch returns a structured output object with bytes, HTTP code, codeText, result, durationMs, and url, and maps the tool_result block content to result only. Go returns ToolResult.Content containing a 'Prompt:' envelope and a Go-specific webfetch_summary_json text block with url/prompt/method/summary/snippets/truncated. It does not expose bytes, status, codeText, duration, or the exact result-only content contract. Input schema strictness also differs: TS uses z.strictObject and url(). Go JSON unmarshalling ignores extra fields and the JSON schema lacks additionalProperties:false or a URL-format marker.

improvement_points.title: HTTP request headers and oversized body handling differ
improvement_points.description: TS asks for markdown first, uses the central WebFetch user agent, and lets axios reject responses over the 10MB maxContentLength. Go sends a browser-like HTML/XML Accept header, a hard-coded ClaudeCode/1.0 user agent, and uses io.LimitReader(10MB) without detecting whether the server sent more bytes. That can change content negotiation and can silently summarize a truncated body as if it were complete.

improvement_points.title: Go preapproved-host matching expands TS allowlist semantics to subdomains
improvement_points.description: TS preapproved matching allows exact hostname-only entries and exact path-prefix entries with segment boundaries. Go additionally treats every hostname-only entry as matching any subdomain suffix. This can bypass permission prompts and switch to preapproved prompt/copyright behavior for hosts that TS would not consider preapproved.

improvement_points.title: URL validation and error surfaces are not TS-equivalent
improvement_points.description: TS validation first checks URL parseability for validateInput, then validateURL in the fetch helper enforces max length, no userinfo, and at least a two-label hostname while relying on HTTPS upgrade and domain preflight for the rest. Go performs DNS lookups before fetch, rejects non-http(s), rejects single-label hosts and private/link-local/loopback resolved IPs, and returns different 'blocked URL' tool errors. This may be intentional hardening, but it is not exact parity and should be either aligned or recorded as an intentional non-parity policy.

improvement_points.title: Existing tests cover many helpers but do not lock the remaining TS-vs-Go production behavior
improvement_points.description: Go has substantial WebFetch tests, but several tests validate helper existence or no-panic behavior rather than TS-equivalent Execute output. Missing or weak coverage includes permission ask/deny/allow, domain_info can_fetch fail-closed behavior, 10-hop redirect success, protocol/port/userinfo redirect rejection, redirect message text, production cache wiring, output object fields, binary summary plus saved-file note, oversized-body rejection, preapproved exact matching, and cancellation during summarisation.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add TS-equivalent WebFetch permission decision lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: WebFetch can produce allow, deny, and ask decisions before Execute using ruleContent domain:<hostname>.
Preapproved hosts auto-allow through the same decision layer.
Ask decisions include an addRules/localSettings suggestion equivalent to TS buildSuggestions.
Existing static AllowedDomains/DisallowedDomains behavior is either mapped into the permission layer or documented as separate managed policy.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align domain_info preflight with TS can_fetch and fail-closed semantics
acceptance_criteria: Production WebFetch runs domain_info by default unless a skipWebFetchPreflight-equivalent setting is true.
The response parser consumes can_fetch exactly like TS and treats can_fetch=false as blocked.
Transport errors, decode failures, and non-200 responses produce a user-visible domain-check failure instead of fail-open.
Only allowed verdicts are cached for 5 minutes; blocked/failed verdicts re-check on the next attempt.
Tests cover allowed, blocked, check_failed, skip setting, cache-hit, and malformed response behavior.

implementation_subtasks.title: Make redirect following and redirect output match TS
acceptance_criteria: Same-origin redirect permission checks protocol, port, userinfo, and hostname-with-www exactly like TS isPermittedRedirect.
The redirect hop cap is 10.
Cross-host redirects return the TS REDIRECT DETECTED block with original URL, redirect URL, status text, and retry parameters.
Cross-host redirect markers are not cached as fetched page content.
Tests cover protocol downgrade, port change, userinfo injection, www add/remove, 10-hop chain, 11-hop failure, relative Location, and cross-host retry message.

implementation_subtasks.title: Replace production WebFetch cache with TS-style raw URL content cache
acceptance_criteria: Execute and SetupRegistry use the typed WebFetchCache or an equivalent cache that stores raw fetched content metadata by original URL only.
Different prompts for the same URL reuse the fetched page but re-run prompt application.
Cache entries carry bytes, status code/text, content type, persisted binary path/size, and markdown content.
Cache enforces 15-minute TTL and 50MB byte cap in the production path.
Redirects and HTTP errors are not cached as successful page content.
A clear-cache lifecycle hook can clear WebFetch cache state.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire prompt application to the secondary model and preserve abort/error semantics
acceptance_criteria: Production WebFetch has a configured secondary-model summariser or provider adapter equivalent to TS queryHaiku.
All non-preapproved-short-markdown content calls the secondary-model path.
Summariser failures are surfaced as tool failures instead of silently falling back to keyword extraction.
Context cancellation during summarisation aborts the tool result and never returns heuristic content.
The offline/CI heuristic fallback is either removed from production Execute or guarded by an explicit test-only/offline mode.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align binary response handling with TS summary-plus-saved-file note
acceptance_criteria: Binary content is persisted with a MIME-derived extension and size metadata.
Binary responses still flow through decoded-content prompt application when TS would do so.
The returned result appends a note matching TS structure: Binary content (<content-type>, <size>) also saved to <path>.
The cache stores persisted path/size metadata and does not replace summaries with marker-only output.
Tests cover PDF-like content, persist success, persist failure, and prompt application on binary responses.

implementation_subtasks.title: Expose the TS WebFetch output object and strict input schema
acceptance_criteria: WebFetch success output carries bytes, code, codeText, result, durationMs, and url with TS-equivalent names and types.
The model-facing tool result content is the processed result string, not a Go-specific Prompt envelope.
Status/duration/bytes are available to renderers or metadata consumers in the same lifecycle point as TS outputSchema.
Input parsing rejects unknown fields for WebFetch and schema advertises strict object behavior; url is declared as a URL string.
Existing Go-specific webfetch_summary_json consumers are either migrated or retained only as compatibility metadata without changing TS-visible output.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align WebFetch HTTP request headers, body-limit behavior, and URL validation policy decisions
acceptance_criteria: Fetch requests prefer markdown with Accept: text/markdown, text/html, */* and use a central WebFetch user-agent equivalent.
Oversized responses over 10MB fail or surface a TS-equivalent error instead of silently reading the first 10MB.
Any URL validation hardening beyond TS is explicitly separated as managed security policy and covered by tests.
HTTP-to-HTTPS upgrade remains TS-compatible before the fetch.
Tests cover content negotiation, over-limit bodies, long URLs, userinfo, single-label hosts, and private/loopback policy behavior.

implementation_subtasks.title: Make preapproved-host matching exact to TS
acceptance_criteria: Hostname-only preapproved entries match only the exact hostname after URL hostname normalization.
Path-scoped entries keep exact path-segment prefix behavior.
Subdomains like typed.docs.python.org and stable.go.dev are not preapproved unless the TS list explicitly contains them.
Tests are updated so expected preapproval behavior is derived from the TS source, not the current Go wildcard extension.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add production-path WebFetch parity tests for the remaining runtime/output gaps
acceptance_criteria: Tests fail on current code for at least: permission ask/deny/allow, domain_info can_fetch fail-closed behavior, protocol/port/userinfo redirect rejection, 10-hop redirect success, output object fields, production cache wiring, binary summary note, oversized body behavior, cancellation during summarisation, and exact preapproved matching.
Tests exercise WebFetchTool.Execute or registry-created tools when feasible, not only helper functions.
Fixture names map each scenario to the TS evidence path and expected normalized output shape.
Each implementation task above can make a small subset of these tests green independently.
WebFetch input validation and schema behavior match the original TS implementation for all report gaps.
WebFetch model-visible output and structured result data match TS golden fixtures.
WebFetch runtime side effects, state transitions, permission decisions, and error branches listed in improvement_points are implemented or explicitly documented as intentionally out of scope.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
